prompt: When does reflective, brightly colored riding gear help other drivers notice you?
choices: On every ride, day or night
Only after dark, when headlights hit it
Only in rain, fog or snow
Only in daytime, when colors show up best
explanation: Wear reflective, bright-colored gear on every ride. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, when bright colors help drivers spot you, and reflective material helps drivers ahead, behind and to the side see you at night.

prompt: You are riding on a high-speed highway and must slow down sharply to turn onto a side road. What should you do before you brake?
choices: Turn on your hazard flashers and coast down
Use only engine braking so you don't startle anyone
Flash your brake light to warn drivers behind you
Look back over your shoulder at the driver behind you
explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is less noticeable than a car's. Flash it before you slow more quickly than others might expect, such as when turning off a high-speed road, or where they may not expect it, like mid-block.
ref: MSF Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 24 (Brake Light)
